National Parliament
National Assembly
Complete Details of Proceedings
26 Magh 2082
Monday
Meeting Number - 7
The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 13:18 hours under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members,
(13:18 hours)
The proceedings of the National Assembly's meeting today commence. Honourable members, names have been received to speak during the 'Zero Hour'. I have allocated 1 minute of time to each Honourable member to speak during the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Goma Devi Timalsina.
Honourable Ms. Goma Devi Timalsina
(Communist Party of Nepal, Unified Socialist)
(13:19 hours)
Right Honourable Chairperson, we Nepalis who have fallen into the quagmire of poverty, today, while going to work in Meghalaya in the eastern hilly region, have faced a disaster in the coal mine tunnel there. Many people have been killed, some have been injured, and some are missing. In a situation where the bodies of those who died cannot be brought back to Nepal, I wish to draw the attention of the government, through the Right Honourable Chairperson, to quickly focus on bringing back the bodies of the deceased to Nepal, providing treatment to the injured, and searching for the missing. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.
(13:20 hours)
Honourable Ms. Jayanti Devi Rai (Communist Party of Nepal, Unified Socialist):
(13:20 hours)
Right Honourable Chairperson, I first pay my heartfelt tribute to the late artist Sunil Thapa and to Dr. Mina Acharya, who has always played a leading role in every change in the women's movement. Along with this, many injured people, including brother Ravi, who were seriously injured in the movement on the 23rd and 24th, are in a very critical condition. Ravi has had his arm amputated after four months of treatment in India. Similarly, there are many other injured people. The situation where it is more difficult to live a thousand times a day than to die has been created, and neither the government nor the protestors have inquired about this. I wish to draw the attention of the government and the protestors to this matter. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Durga Gurung.
(13:29 hours)
Honourable Mr. Durga Gurung (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson,
(13:21 hours)
On behalf of the Nepali Congress, I offer my heartfelt tribute to the late Baldev Bohara, who was elected to the National Assembly from Sudurpashchim Province, and express my deep condolences to his family members. Honourable Chairperson, the public is disappointed due to the halt in development programs. Although the development budget allocated by the previous government was supposed to be operational from July, due to the protests on September 9th and 10th, all projects have been halted by the current government. This has caused many problems for the people of the affected areas as plans for roads, health, education, and drinking water, which are used in daily life, have been stopped. I wish to draw the attention of the government, through the Right Honourable Chairperson, that no government should stop development plans for the people. Thank you. Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Nar Bahadur Bisht.
(13:22 hours)
Honourable Mr. Nar Bahadur Bisht (Communist Party of Nepal, Maoist Centre):
(13:23 hours)
Right Honourable Chairperson, I first wish to offer my heartfelt tribute to the late Honourable Baldev Bohara, and I want to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal that the election to be held on February 15th should be conducted freely and without any malpractice. I wish to make a special request for this. The election of February 15th is currently underway across the country. Elections are being held in 165 constituencies across the country, but in Jhapa, in particular, there is concern about whether the election will be held or not due to two extremist groups, and whether this will lead to clashes. Therefore, I urge the state to take timely precautions against that extremism. I wish for the election to be held on February 15th to be conducted freely, without malpractice, and impartially, so that all Nepali citizens can exercise their right to vote, and I hope the state will ensure this. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar.
(13:24 hours)
Honourable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Communist Party of Nepal, Maoist Centre):
(13:24 hours)
Chairperson, the shortage of consumer goods and the price increase are steadily rising in the market. Why is this happening just before the election? There is a shortage of gas, and the prices of food items like cooking oil and salt are increasing. I demand that the government immediately monitor the market and take action to control the price increase. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima".
(13:24 hours)
Honourable Ms. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Communist Party of Nepal, Unified Socialist):
(13:24 hours)
Right Honourable Chairperson, I wish to express my heartfelt condolences to the economist, historical figure Dr. Mina Acharya, and National Assembly member Baldev Bohora. Right Honourable Chairperson, on the night of January 25th, a passenger bus traveling from Ward No. 7 to Ward No. 8 of Pulchoki Rural Municipality in Baitadi met with an accident, resulting in the tragic death of 13 people, including the bride's brother. 45 people are injured, and all except the bride's brother are from the same village. I express my sorrow over this unimaginable incident. I offer my heartfelt tribute to all the deceased and wish for the speedy recovery of all the injured. Such incidents are not uncommon on the hilly roads of Sudurpashchim. These tragic incidents continue to occur due to the negligence of drivers and the non-compliance with traffic rules. I wish to ask the government, through the Right Honourable Chairperson, when the roads in Sudurpashchim will stop being death traps. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Yuvraj Sharma.
(13:25 hours)
Honourable Mr. Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress): Honourable
(13:26 hours)
Chairperson, the Prime Minister and ministers, while holding office and being candidates themselves, have never questioned the impartiality of past elections as much as it is being questioned today. The senior leader, Kisunji, never forgot that even though he was defeated in an election held by his own government, he made the country, the people, and democracy victorious. That was the height of impartiality. In the past, governments were cautious even with the Non-Aligned foreign policy and the One-China policy. Is the current government not trying to mess up everything? There is concern everywhere. Right Honourable Chairperson, it is not enough to simply make a name in history as the first female prime minister; one must also succeed in creating history. The puppet show of the helpless and powerless was seen yesterday as well. Today, the sole demand of the people is for impartial elections, which is also a citizen's right. For this, the unity and firm stance of the proponents of the current constitution are now necessary. In conclusion, I offer my heartfelt tribute to Honourable Baldev Bohora. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.
(13:27 hours)
Honourable Ms. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Communist Party of Nepal, Unified Socialist):
(13:27 hours)
Right Honourable Chairperson, I wish to discuss the issue of health insurance in the health sector. It has been reported that private hospitals that have taken health insurance have not received payments from the government for a long time, and there are rumors that the government is preparing new health insurance criteria. This rumor is adding despair rather than energy to people working in the health sector. The government should not do anything that causes despair to the public. There should be no confusion for the public; I want to draw attention to this. Another matter is that we hear about heart attack incidents almost daily. We hear about them from the east and the west without a single day passing without them. Why is this happening? I want this to be investigated. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.
(13:28 hours)
Honourable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Communist Party of Nepal, Maoist Centre):
(13:28 hours)
Right Honourable Chairperson, some people are sitting here intending to bring a political tsunami to this country. Whether a political tsunami will come or not, we don't know. We don't know if that tsunami will sweep only them or others too. We will have to wait until February 15th for that. Similarly, some people want to eat something, and some people want to eat that. We don't know if that person can eat it or not. And we don't know if the people feeding them can feed that person or not. After eating, what will that person do? Will they leave it and wander around? We don't know that either. For all of this, Right Honourable Chairperson, we will have to wait for the election to be held on February 15th. All this talk of a political tsunami, whether that person can eat something or not, all of this will be judged on February 15th. We are waiting for that. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the time for Honourable members to speak during the Zero Hour concludes here. Honourable members, I would like to inform you that there will be no Special Time in today's meeting of the National Assembly. Honourable members, one-third of the Honourable members have completed their six-year term as per the constitutional provision and will be bidding farewell from February 19, 2082. Some Honourable members have requested time to speak on their experiences gained during their tenure in the assembly and committees, as well as on contemporary issues. Since the experiences of the Honourable members may be useful in the future, we will provide time for the Honourable members to present their experiences. For this, I have set a time limit of 12 minutes for each Honourable member. First, Honourable Member Dr. Beduram Bhusal.
Honourable Dr. Beduram Bhusal (Communist Party of Nepal, Unified Socialist):
(13:31 hours)
Right Honourable Chairperson, thank you very much for the special time today to share experiences. It is very difficult to narrate all six years of experience in these 12 minutes. Therefore, I have decided to read a concise written speech today, as I have never given a written speech in this assembly for the past six years. I seek permission for this. Right Honourable Chairperson, I wish to briefly present my experiences and feelings from working in this assembly for six years as follows:
1. Joining and Expectations in the Assembly: I joined this assembly on February 12, 2080. When I joined this assembly, I had two types of expectations. These expectations were expressed in my first speech in the assembly on February 12, 2080.
1. Considering the reality that the country cannot move forward because economic, social, and cultural transformation has not occurred in line with the political changes in the country, this assembly needs to work.
2. This assembly is a deliberative assembly. This deliberative assembly must take initiatives to mitigate the problems faced by the country and move the country forward in the right direction. I have been present in the assembly in line with these expectations. Looking back as the term is about to end, it seems that this assembly has generally worked as a deliberative assembly, but the campaign for economic, social, and cultural transformation in the country has not been undertaken at all, which was the appropriate time when I advocated for launching an economic-social and cultural transformation campaign. At that time, the Communist Party of Nepal (CPN), in which I myself was involved...

There was a government with a two-thirds majority. That government could have launched the campaign but did not. As the then government did not work in accordance with the party's policy and public expectations, a serious dispute arose within the party. Consequently, the party unity broke and the government also fell. Later, various types of governments were formed, but the governments formed later also could not launch economic, social, and cultural transformation campaigns in the country as expected. Employment opportunities could not be created for the people, nor could corruption control and good governance be guaranteed. Continuous voices were raised, but no work was done. Therefore, as the term is ending and we are about to depart, we have to repeat the same things. 2. Work details of 6 years: In the 6-year tenure, for about one year, we could not work openly due to the outbreak of the Coronavirus. For another year, we could not work due to obstruction from the then opposition. For about one year, I was also engaged in the regular work of this assembly as I held the responsibility of the Minister of Agriculture and Livestock Development of the Government of Nepal. For the remaining time, I was fully active in the work of the assembly. I have been rarely absent from assembly meetings, and my attendance in the meetings of the committee I was in is about 90 percent. I was most active in lawmaking. Wherever I was in a committee, it was in the Legislative Management Committee. During my time in the committee, I participated in the theoretical and clause-wise discussions of 48 bills and expressed my views. For about 6 months, from Bhadra 23, 2079 to Chaitra 16, I worked as the Chairperson of the Legislative Management Committee. During that period, I presented three committee reports related to bills and one annual report to the assembly. I formed a subcommittee to study how many laws to be made according to the constitution have been made and how many have not been made, and worked to guide it. While in the committee, 6 post-legislative reviews of laws and 2 research and study works were also done. I worked as the coordinator of the subcommittee formed to study the implementation status of the remaining laws to be made according to the constitution and presented the report to the committee. Apart from the work done in the committee, I participated in the discussions of four budget principles and priorities and four budget discussions in the assembly and expressed my views. I participated in the discussions of three annual policies and programs and expressed my views. I took special time seven times to express my views on contemporary issues. I expressed my views during zero hour four times and during emergency hour once. I participated in the discussions of two resolutions and expressed my views. I presented one non-governmental bill in the assembly. I gave speeches on the occasion of the commencement of the assembly session five times and on the occasion of the conclusion of the session once. I addressed the assembly once in the capacity of a minister. I gave welcome and best wishes speeches to the newly elected members of the assembly twice. I supported the candidacy in the election of the Speaker once and gave congratulatory and best wishes speeches to the elected Speaker. In summary, these are the works I have done during my tenure in this assembly. 3. Experiences and Feelings: In the six-year tenure, I have gained various experiences and feelings. It is not possible to present them in detail here, so I want to present them briefly in the following points. First - I entered this assembly as a member of the parliamentary party of the then Communist Party of Nepal (CPN). After the CPN split, I wanted to register as an independent MP but could not. After that, I served as the leader of the National Assembly parliamentary party of CPN (Unified Socialist). Now, as I am about to depart, I am serving as the leader of the National Assembly parliamentary party of the Communist Party of Nepal. I believe this is an unforgettable experience for me. Second - In the National Assembly, work is generally done with consensus without political tug-of-war like in the House of Representatives. This is another pleasant experience and feeling. Third - In the process of discussing and passing bills in the assembly or committee, there has been consensus except for exceptions, and except for special circumstances, party whips have not been applied in the discussion and passage of bills. I believe this is another positive experience. Fourth - In the context of lawmaking, some good traditions and standards have been established, and many very important laws have been made. As a lawmaker, I have taken this as a positive experience and feeling. Fifth - Our bureaucracy has not yet been freed from traditional beliefs. As a result, some aspects of our laws still follow a traditional structure and pattern. I have taken this as a negative experience and feeling. 4. Types and Amendments of Bills: Due to the lack of uniformity in the structure and subject matter of bills coming from the government, it is difficult to discuss and amend them. Therefore, the Legislative Management Committee of the National Assembly, through its special initiative, enacted the Federal Parliament Legislative Act, 2081. That act clearly directs what the structure of a bill should be, what subjects should be included in an act, what subjects should not be included, what subjects can be delegated, and what subjects cannot be delegated. However, bills are still coming with even substantive matters delegated. The Legislative Management Committee has not fully followed the Legislative Act. Generally, the following three types of bills come to the assembly. 1. Bills to enact new laws, 2. Bills to amend and consolidate old laws, and 3. Bills to amend only some clauses of old laws. Among these three types of bills, for bills to enact new laws and bills to amend and consolidate old laws, all clauses, whether amendment proposals have been submitted or not, are discussed openly, and passed with necessary amendments if deemed necessary. However, in the case of bills brought to amend only some clauses of old laws, only the clauses proposed for amendment are discussed, and necessary amendments are made. 5. Establishment of Good Traditions and Standards: Our National Assembly has established some good traditions and standards. All committees of the National Assembly are doing excellent work within their respective areas of work. However, from the perspective that the main job of the parliament is lawmaking, it would not be an exaggeration to say that the Legislative Management Committee has done the best work. It has also established some standards for lawmaking. I would like to present the good traditions established by the National Assembly and the standards established by the Legislative Management Committee in the following points. 1. Conducting assembly and committee meetings on time without any deviation, and speakers also finishing their remarks within the allotted time. 2. Working with a fixed term. 3. Conducting clause-wise discussions of bills only in the presence of the concerned minister. 4. Discussing with stakeholders before conducting clause-wise discussions of bills. 5. Specifying the date of commencement of the act. 6. Not delegating substantive matters in laws. 7. Making provisions for measuring the implementation of laws. Some Suggestions for the Assembly Mr. Chairman, finally, I would like to conclude with a few suggestions. My suggestions are as follows. 1. The assembly should maintain the good traditions and standards established so far and continue to establish more good traditions and standards in the future. 2. This assembly should continue to be an assembly that works with its own identity, not as a mere shadow of the House of Representatives. With these suggestions, I wish to conclude. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Indira Devi Gautam. (13:41 hrs) Honorable Mr. Indira Devi Gautam (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Mr. Chairman, first of all, I would like to pay heartfelt tribute to the Honorable Member Baldev Bohara of the National Assembly. Similarly, I would also like to pay heartfelt tribute to the economist Mina Acharya. Mr. Chairman, the experiences I have gained from this esteemed house over 6 years are detailed here. It has been a significant and glorious experience in my political life to have had the opportunity to serve as a member of this esteemed house for 6 years. During this period, I had the opportunity to closely observe and understand various aspects of legislation, government oversight, policy making, parliamentary decorum, and public accountability. During my tenure in this assembly, I was able to participate in the process of discussing, amending, and passing bills for federal lawmaking. It is also my responsibility to participate in suggesting and amending bills by keeping in mind the rights of the provinces, the role of local levels, inclusivity, social justice, and the spirit of the constitution. Therefore, economic, social, and administrative reforms have been important learning experiences for me. Among the committees formed under the National Assembly, by being in the Committee on Federalism Strengthening and National Concerns, I had the opportunity to play a role in policy analysis, monitoring government activities, matters of public interest, various issues of national concern, federalism implementation, and coordination among all three tiers. The discussions in the committee helped me understand the gap between the laws made on paper and their practical implementation. In this process, I got the opportunity to clearly experience the responsibility of the parliament by making ministries accountable, discussing and reviewing budget implementation, and raising the grievances of stakeholders through parliamentary means. In the 6-year tenure, I have raised and am raising public problems, sectoral demands, and issues of national concern with the government through special time and zero hour. This has made me realize that the parliament has the main responsibility of making laws and is also a constitutional check to keep the government on the right track. However, the extent to which the suggestions given have been implemented needs honest self-reflection by the concerned bodies. Mr. Chairman, this assembly must play an important role by giving special attention to the geographical diversity and inequality seen in the development of our country. I have had the opportunity to deeply learn the culture of consensus and respect by collaborating and discussing with experienced senior political personalities and honorable members from diverse backgrounds in the National Assembly. We should all agree that the practice of reaching common conclusions on national issues even amidst disagreements lays the foundation for strengthening democratic culture. Mr. Chairman, this assembly has been able to do many good things in 6 years, and many of those good things have been presented here, and we have been raising them during special time and zero hour. In the course of 6 years of experience, a serious problem that I have repeatedly felt is that the failure to implement many important suggestions, directives, and resolutions raised by the National Assembly has raised questions about the dignity and effectiveness of the National Assembly. The legal provision to compel the implementation of resolutions, proposals, suggestions, and directives passed by the assembly is weak. I have felt that these are taken only as advice. The ministries also did not seem serious about this. The time limit for implementation was not set, nor was the progress report sought with interest. The issues raised in the discussions of the National Assembly were not given priority by the ministers and ministries. I have found the oversight role of the parliament to be weak. I have felt that the suggestions of this assembly are taken only as a formality. I have found many suggestions raised in the assembly to be entangled in party equations, power dynamics, and the political activities of the ruling and opposition parties, and national issues are also caught in party disputes.

The committees have been shrinking. They prepare good reports, and it seems there is no permanent mechanism to monitor the implementation of those reports. Reports are just piled up, or do the ministries even look at them?

Mr. Chairperson, regarding the implementation of directives from the Committee Report Resolution Proposal, it appears necessary to set a deadline for implementation and to arrange for clarification in the Parliament if a report is not implemented. If a system were in place to provide the House with a self-assessment report after each session, detailing which suggestions were implemented, which were not, and why, perhaps there would be more interest in implementation. The suggestions made by the National Assembly were and are important, but I feel the implementation system is weak due to a lack of sincerity in the implementation aspect.

Mr. Chairperson, everyone is aware that prosperity, development, and democracy cannot be strengthened without the coordination of political will, administrative integrity, and public awareness. However, the incident that arose from the dissatisfaction of August 14-15, 2025, causing pain that will never be erased or forgotten. That rebellion was raised with demands for good governance, ethical conduct, an end to corruption, and the release of social activists. But were those demands alone justified? And did the Nepali people want such chaos and terrorism? We all need to reflect on why and how such a situation arose. A serious review is needed. We had to endure unimaginable events. Children and youth lost their lives, causing irreparable damage. Historical structures of the state were destroyed. Let us all be aware that such a terrible situation never repeats itself.

Mr. Chairperson, some parliamentary meetings have been like political party propaganda, with honorable members criticizing other parties and making comments that create despair among the public. The Parliament seemed to be preoccupied with accusations and counter-accusations. How much attention have we paid to the respect and dignity of the House? A very serious issue has arisen: the Parliament must be able to make, and has made, quality, timely, and practical laws that benefit the nation and the people, but not all have been completed. When making laws, did we prioritize the voice of the people, the needs of the country, and the spirit of the constitution? Our role is crucial in preparing plans for long-term thinking on issues of national independence, sovereignty, social justice, good governance, and prosperity, and in making the executive branch capable and accountable. But how has it been? Although the Parliament is theoretically powerful, its practical state appears relatively weak. Due to insufficient discussion and under government pressure, some laws of low quality have been hastily introduced, drawing widespread criticism. Some laws have been made to suit political interests rather than being practical, leading to contradictions between laws. Some laws have become outdated. Many essential laws have not yet been made. The main job of the Parliament is to make laws in accordance with the constitution, creating an easy and transparent environment for people to work. But our work process is very weak, slow, and cumbersome. The Constitution of Nepal gives the Parliament the main authority to make laws, but in practice, it has not been effective or of quality, which I feel is a great deficiency. Only in some aspects.

Finally, I express my gratitude to my party, the CPN (UML), Koshi Province, the former voters who gave me the responsibility of the role of MP in this esteemed House, the honorable MPs who supported me in various situations, the civil servants, the secretary and all the staff of the committee who worked day and night with diligence to make the committee effective, the security agencies, the journalist friends, and all well-wishers who have been supportive. With the expectation of continued support, I would like to say thank you. My six years of experience... some might say only negative things have come up, but many positive things have also been expressed here. This House has done many good things, and I have brought up these points to draw attention to some shortcomings so that special attention can be paid to these matters in the future. Former honorable members have already presented many good practices and new practices in this House. Therefore, this esteemed House will fulfill the needs given by our constitution and the expectations, rights, and aspirations of the people in a systematic and dignified manner, and perhaps we will not have to welcome the honorable members who will come in the future. Therefore, I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the elected honorable members in the National Assembly, as I am currently in this situation, and I believe they will complete the remaining tasks and lead this country towards prosperity and improve the lives of the people. With this belief, I once again greet all the honorable members and end my remarks. Thank you.

Presiding: Honorable Vice-Chairperson Ms. Bimla Ghimire.
(13:53 hrs)
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Maya Prasad Sharma.
(13:54 hrs)

Honorable Mr. Maya Prasad Sharma (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):
(13:54 hrs)
-
Honorable Chairperson, I express my heartfelt condolences to senior journalist Sunil Thapa and Dr. artist Sunil Thapa and Dr. Mina Acharya. Honorable Chairperson, I have tried to cover the positive and negative aspects of the last six years as much as possible. I wish to share my thoughts and experiences of the work done during my six-year tenure. With gratitude for the active and meaningful role of the honorable members who completed their two-year terms and departed, they were bid farewell with good wishes on Falgun 19, 2076. Similarly, we new members of Parliament were welcomed on the 29th of the same month, and we took our oaths in the name of the people. It is a long-held belief that one must have a clear perspective when taking on party work or state responsibilities, but any responsibility is not just taken for the sake of taking it; one must be able to skillfully face its importance and challenges. With this goal, there was strong self-confidence that the responsibility could be fulfilled. When I took the oath of office as a member of the National Assembly, I had not imagined that so much could be done. At that time, the CPN (UML) and the CPN (Maoist) parties had united to form the CPN. Since the party was in government, there was full confidence that some new work could be done, but that situation could not continue for long. Nevertheless, I feel that we have established a good tradition in the National Assembly. Since coming to the National Assembly, I have had the opportunity to collaborate with two honorable chairpersons, three honorable vice-chairpersons, two secretaries-general, and three National Assembly secretaries. I have felt that the collaboration with them has been very strong due to everyone's effective capability, efficiency, and coordinating role. The National Assembly meetings have been conducted on time, and when discussing any issue, it has been important work to rise above party prejudice and reach conclusions in discussions with greater loyalty to the nation, the people, and national interests. Bills presented in the House, resolution proposals, reports from thematic committees, and other reports have been advanced with consensus, cooperation, and participation, unanimously. I feel that the work of the committees, including playing a coordinating role and conducting meetings with a calendar to visit constituencies in all provinces with programs, and discussing the reports prepared during the thematic study and monitoring by the committee in the House, are very positive aspects.

The resolution proposal of the Parliamentary Special Committee for Study and Monitoring of Federalism Implementation, formed by the National Assembly on Jestha 5, 2079, was unanimously passed by the Parliament on Jestha 19, 2079. I have felt that the proposal passed by the National Assembly has become a milestone for federal strengthening and implementation. The positive role played by the honorable chairperson, party leaders, all honorable members, the secretary-general, and the secretariat staff in overcoming the deadlock caused by the recent youth movement, and the positive understanding of the honorable Prime Minister and honorable ministers towards the National Assembly, have resulted in us being able to stand here and share our experiences and hear each other's experiences. This is the most important thing for now. Honorable Chairperson, since being elected, I first stood up in the National Assembly meeting on Chaitra 3, 2076, and presented my experiences and goals. Even after six years, I see them dimly.

I have mostly expressed my views during special time, zero hour, urgent time, and provincial time. In the absence of Parliament on Shrawan 17, 2077, I had the opportunity to work for two years in the then Sustainable Development and Good Governance Committee as per the ordinance issued by the Honorable Chairperson of the National Assembly. I feel that the work learned and taught in that committee have been important cornerstones of my life. On Bhadra 23, 2079, I was elected as the chairperson of the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee, which has now been renamed, and on Bhadra 31, 2081, I was re-elected as the chairperson of the same committee. The increasing responsibility in the committee where I myself am the chairperson was important in my committee. I feel that the role played by the honorable members in my committee has been historic and memorable. My committee held approximately 175 meetings, but no meeting had to be adjourned due to lack of quorum or disputes. I have always felt that the support of the committee members has been remarkable. Although it felt somewhat incomplete or unfinished when important members working in the committee moved to other responsibilities, positive steps were being taken to resolve it. The committee aimed to simplify, facilitate, and make the work result-oriented through four sub-committees. Regarding public policy, study reports related to national interests have been discussed and passed in the House, while issues related to library policy are under discussion. Regarding delegated legislation, studies were conducted on the Tribhuvan University Act, 2049, and the Immigration Act, 2049, and these have been presented and discussed in the House. Regarding government assurances, studies have been conducted on the implementation and shortcomings of assurances given by the concerned ministry or stakeholders and the government, and reports have been compiled. I am very happy to have conducted in-depth studies with the participation of experts and scholars, along with exploring and conducting field studies of documents, records of national importance, and historical and archaeological subjects. Another important thing is that, through the initiative of our committee, the Bill Act, 2081, has been passed by both houses and is in the process of implementation, which has greatly helped in organizing delegated legislation.

Through the initiative of the honorable members of our committee, along with the resolution proposal on dignified menstruation to make citizens' lives safe, quality, and secure, and regarding so-called Dalit communities...

Discussion, single or joint, with concerned parties on issues of policy and law related to rights.
Regarding the issues related to compensation for the earthquake centered in Jajarkot and Doti, funds have been provided in two phases for the construction of temporary shelters, along with the work of providing assurances with the presence of the then Prime Minister and Ministers after discussing the report after conducting field study. With the change of government, the delay in formulating the work procedures, the excuse of an increased number of houses, and the confusion in the name of DPR have caused the people there to suffer immensely. The citizen government formed since the youth movement, along with this issue and its related concerns, the elections within the declared time, the security situation, the work done for its arrangements, and discussions related to development construction were held. The committee has felt that it has played an important role in facilitating the environment by discussing, interacting, and consulting with the Provincial Assemblies and local levels in the selected sites of all seven provinces, especially in two provinces, amidst difficult circumstances and limited resources for their respective thematic tasks. Along with policy and law formulation, efforts have been continuously made to make the law practical, inclusive, and effective through active participation in the study, discussion, and amendment process of bills.
